# The same settlement as `fx_usd_invoice_settled_into_an_hkd_bank.txt`, stating
# the rate instead of the figure that landed. `share_price:` and
# `settled_amount:` are the two documented spellings of one fact — 100 USD at
# 7.80 is the 780.00 HKD the other file states outright — so a book built from
# either must be the same book, and a file refused under one spelling must be
# refused under the other.
#
# It carries the other document's memo because it describes the other
# document's movement — which is what a reader hand-writing a second block
# against money the book already holds would copy. The duplicate guard matches
# on the memo, so a block that named a different one would be a different
# payment and rightly not compared.
customer "C-US"
	name: "US Customer"
	currency: USD

invoice "INV-USD-BY-RATE"
	customer_id: "C-US"
	currency: USD
	date_opened: 2026-01-05
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-05
		description: "Consulting"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-01-05
		due: 2026-02-05
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
		memo: "Invoice INV-USD-BY-RATE"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		date: 2026-02-25
		amount: 100
		account: "Assets:Bank:HKD"
		share_price: 7.80
		txn_guid: "TXN_GUID"
		memo: "Payment for INV-USD-INTO-HKD"
		Income:FX Gain $residual$ CAD
